column1: # The eight central banks' policy rates, January 2000 to December 2025 (XR4; spec-exchange-rates 3.8, star 11).
# Each line is a change: the money, the month it took effect (a decision announced and in force in that month),
# and the rate after it, percent a year. A month's rate is the last change at or before it: the rate at the
# month's end, so two changes in one month leave the second. The first line of each money is January 2000's.
# Transcribed from each bank's announced decisions, as the BIS's central bank policy rates (CBPOL) carry them,
#   USD  the Federal Reserve's federal funds target; a target range (since December 2008) at its midpoint.
#   EUR  the ECB's main refinancing rate to December 2008; its deposit facility rate from January 2009, when the
#        ECB's full allotment put the euro's overnight rate at the deposit floor (EONIA, then the euro short-term rate).
#   JPY  the Bank of Japan's guidance for the overnight call rate (0 under the zero-rate and quantitative policies,
#        0.05 for "0 to 0.1%"); the rate on the policy-rate balance, -0.1%, from February 2016 to March 2024.
#   GBP  the Bank of England's Bank Rate.
#   CNY  the People's Bank of China's one-year benchmark lending rate, and from August 2019 the one-year loan prime rate.
#   CAD  the Bank of Canada's target for the overnight rate.
#   AUD  the Reserve Bank of Australia's cash rate target.
#   CHF  the Swiss National Bank's target for three-month franc Libor (the range's middle, or the rate it said it
#        aimed at) to June 2019, and its policy rate from then.
